messages:
Anya: Quick heads-up — customer 'Lyra' LoRA merge into gptx-base-int4 produced a weird token shift after quant. Quick-eval pack (200 cases) shows a 5-8% drop in QA F1 and a bump in hallucinations. Repro steps below.

Bhavin: Can you paste the exact merge command + tokenizer info? Also which quant tool (bitsandbytes / llama.cpp / custom)?

Anya: Command I used:
```bash
./tools/merge_lora.py \
  --base checkpoints/gptx-base-fp16.safetensors \
  --lora checkpoints/lyra_cust_lora.safetensors \
  --out builds/lyra_gptx_merged_fp16.safetensors \
  --quant 4 \
  --rescale True
```
tokenizer: lyra-tokenizer v0.2 (we added a special token `<|cust|>` during finetune). Quant pipeline: our internal quantizer (4-bit, per-channel symmetric blocks).

Mika: Sounds like a tokenizer vocab mismatch is likely — LoRA trained with v0.2 that includes `<|cust|>`. If the base tokenizer lacks it, embeddings shift to adjacent ids and behaviour changes. Also possible quant rounding during direct merge. :mag:

Priya: @Anya can you try forcing a tokenizer merge first (`--force-tokenizer-merge`) and run a 200-case smoke eval? Keep seed small for reproducibility.

Anya: EvalBot already ran the quick pack before I started the triage.

EvalBot: Auto-eval summary: dataset=lyra_smoke_200 | metric=qa_f1: base=0.876 -> merged=0.812 (-6.4%) | halluc_rate: base=0.03 -> merged=0.09 | avg_resp_len: base=42 -> merged=28. Full details: https://internal-evals/redwood/2845012345/summary.html

Bhavin: Ok that's non-trivial. Two leading hypotheses: (1) tokenizer misalign (2) quantization/rescale issue when merging into an already-quantized checkpoint. InfraBot, any known caveats with merging LoRA into our 4-bit checkpoints?

InfraBot: Known behaviour: our 4-bit quant engine uses blockwise symmetric quantization. If LoRA weights are merged directly into a 4-bit checkpoint without fp16 merge/rescale, you can get large negative/positive spikes after re-quantization. Workarounds:
- merge into fp16 first (merge_in_fp16=True), then run our canonical quantize pipeline (fp16 -> 8bit -> 4bit)
- enable `rescale=True` during merge with per-channel normalization
- or perform merge + per-channel clip/repair before final quantize

Priya: To isolate token vs quant, can you run: (A) merge -> fp16 -> eval, (B) merge->fp16->quantize(8)->eval, (C) quantize(4) as final and eval. If fp16 merge mirrors base, then quant is culprit.

Anya: Running that now. I'll: 1) merge into fp16 (no quant) 2) run smoke eval 3) run our 8->4 quant pipeline and re-eval. Posting logs when done.

Bhavin: Please add `--seed=42 --disable-cache` to the eval harness so results are deterministic. Also include the small set of failing prompts in the thread so we can debug tokenization effects.

Mika: Also check `tokenizer.json` diffs — if special tokens were appended, token ids shift. Add a quick sanity check in the onboarding script that compares `len(tokenizer.vocab)` and `special_tokens_map` between base and LoRA-training tokenizer.

Anya: Quick update: merged fp16 run finished. Summary: fp16 merged = base baseline (qa_f1 delta -0.5%). After our canonical 8->4 quant pipeline the merged model drops to -1.8%. Direct merge->4 (what I originally did) was -6.4%. So root cause is quant rounding when merging straight into 4-bit checkpoints. Logs: https://artifacts/internal/2845012345/log.txt

Priya: Great repro. Action items: (A) update docs with recommended flow: merge fp16 -> canonical quantize (8->4) (B) add `--force-tokenizer-merge` flag and explicit tokenizer-sanity check to merge tool (C) run full 2k eval for prod gating on Lyra.

Bhavin: I'll open a small PR for the merge script and add CI smoke tests that re-run this scenario.

Mika: I'll add a checklist item in onboarding: "tokenizer version match" + small prompt divergence test.

Anya: I'll run the 2k overnight with `--seed=42` and post the eval link tomorrow morning. Also will attach the mini failing prompts as requested.

Priya: Great, thanks team. Marking this triaged. :white_check_mark:
